name: deputy-mcp

tools.name: browser_capabilities
tools.description: The full contract of every open tab: each form as a typed tool with its JSON Schema (types, allowed values, min/max, required fields), what those fields currently hold, and every button and link with a ref you can click. This is what you read instead of a screenshot — it is complete, so you should not need to probe. Long pages return a window of their links: the reply always states the true total, and you can narrow with actionQuery or page with actionOffset.

actionQuery.description: Only return buttons/links whose label contains this text. Use it when you know what you want.

actionOffset.description: Skip this many actions, for paging through a long list.

tools.name: browser_invoke
tools.description: Call one of the tools browser_capabilities listed, with arguments matching its inputSchema. This acts in the real logged-in browser: it fills and submits the actual form.

tool.description: Tool name exactly as browser_capabilities reported it.

tools.name: browser_fill
tools.description: Set a single field to a value, addressed by the ref browser_capabilities gave it. Use this on pages Deputy could not graft into a typed tool — apps that build a form out of divs, or inputs sitting outside any <form>. For a checkbox pass "true"/"false"; for a <select> pass an option value or its visible text. When a typed tool exists, browser_invoke is better.

ref.description: Field ref from browser_capabilities actions, e.g. "a13".

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click something browser_capabilities listed under "actions", by its ref.

tools.name: browser_read
tools.description: Return the page as plain text for you to read yourself. Use browser_ask instead when you only need one fact: with a model (Deputy Pro or OPENROUTER_API_KEY) Deputy reads the page and answers in a sentence. Use this when you genuinely need the content to reason over.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Point a tab at a URL and wait for it to load, or move through its history with action "back" / "forward", or "reload" it. Deputy re-reads what the new page can do, so call browser_capabilities afterwards to see the tools that appeared.

action.description: Instead of a URL: move through history, or reload.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: Work with browser tabs. "list" shows every tab; "open" opens a URL in a new tab and makes it active; "select" makes a tab active (other tools act on the active tab by default); "close" closes one.

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Wait until text appears, text disappears, or an element becomes visible — for pages that load content after the fact (search results, spinners, SPAs). With no condition, waits timeoutMs. Fails with a clear message on timeout.

text.description: Wait until this text is on the page.

textGone.description: Wait until this text is gone (e.g. "Loading…").

selector.description: Wait until an element matching this CSS selector is visible.

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this long (default 10000, max 60000).

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot and return the image to you. An image costs you roughly 1,000-1,600 tokens, so use it when you need to SEE something: visual or frontend work, layout and styling, charts, images, canvas. For facts on a page prefer browser_ask or browser_read; to act, prefer browser_capabilities. fullPage stitches the whole scrollable page, including anything off the right edge (costs more). ref or selector captures a single element whole, even one wider or taller than the viewport.

fullPage.description: Capture the whole scrollable page, not just the viewport.

ref.description: Capture only this element (a ref from browser_capabilities).

selector.description: Capture only the first element matching this CSS selector.

format.description: jpeg (default, small) or png (sharper text, much larger).

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Find elements by visible text, role (button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, option, heading, tab, menuitem, dialog, img, row, cell) or CSS selector. Returns refs you can pass to browser_act, browser_inspect or browser_screenshot, with label, state and value. Reaches inside forms, open and closed shadow roots, and elements off screen.

text.description: Visible text or accessible name to match (substring, case-insensitive).

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Do one thing to an element: click, double_click, right_click, hover, focus, type (value; replaces unless append), press (keys like "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "ArrowDown", "Control+a"; without a target, presses on the focused element), check, uncheck, select (value = option label or value, native or custom dropdown), clear, scroll_into_view. Typing is sent key by key so autocompletes react. The result reports any dialog or error the action caused. For whole forms, prefer browser_invoke with the typed tool.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_find or browser_capabilities.

selector.description: CSS selector, if you have no ref.

value.description: Text to type, or the option to select.

append.description: For type: add to the existing text instead of replacing it.

acceptDialog.description: Accept the confirm/prompt dialog this action opens (dialogs are dismissed by default).

dialogText.description: With acceptDialog: what to type into a prompt.

steps.description: Several actions in order, in one call (e.g. open a dropdown, pick an option, press Join). Stops at the first that fails.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page (or an element) down/up, by pixels, or to top/bottom. untilStable keeps scrolling to the bottom while an infinite feed keeps loading, and reports how much it grew. Finds the real scroll container in app layouts where the window itself does not scroll.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_find or browser_capabilities.

selector.description: CSS selector, if you have no ref.

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Drag one element onto another (HTML5 drag-and-drop, or pointer-driven libraries such as kanban boards).

tools.name: browser_upload
tools.description: Attach local files (absolute paths, 25 MB total) to a file input, or drop them onto a drop zone.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_find or browser_capabilities.

selector.description: CSS selector, if you have no ref.

tools.name: browser_inspect
tools.description: With a ref or selector: the element's box model, position, computed CSS (or the properties you name), flex/grid layout, visibility, text contrast, overflow, and what is covering it. With no target: a layout audit of the whole page — horizontal overflow and its culprits, clipped text, broken images, missing alt text, small tap targets, low-contrast text, layout shift, fonts. Numbers instead of a screenshot, for CSS debugging.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_find or browser_capabilities.

selector.description: CSS selector, if you have no ref.

tools.name: browser_extract
tools.description: Turn a table, or a repeated list (search results, product cards, feed items), into JSON rows; or list the links. kind "auto" picks the biggest table, else the biggest repeated list. Scope it with a ref or selector. Pair with browser_scroll untilStable for infinite feeds.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_find or browser_capabilities.

selector.description: CSS selector, if you have no ref.

tools.name: browser_console
tools.description: Console messages and page errors: uncaught exceptions with stacks, unhandled rejections, failed resources, and console output from when an agent started driving the tab. Filter by levels (error, warn, info, log, debug). Browser-internal messages (CSP, CORS) are not visible without the debugger.

tools.name: browser_network
tools.description: Requests the page made: method, URL, status, time, type, size, for fetch/XHR and every resource (documents, scripts, styles, images). failedOnly shows 4xx/5xx and network errors. includeBodies adds text/JSON response bodies (first 4 KB) captured while an agent drives the tab.

tools.name: browser_dialog
tools.description: Decide how alert/confirm/prompt dialogs are answered on a tab you are driving. By default they are dismissed (a confirm returns false) and reported in the action result. Call this BEFORE the action that opens the dialog: accept for the next dialog, persist to keep answering that way.

text.description: What to type into a prompt.

tools.name: browser_resize
tools.description: Set the page viewport to a width and height in CSS pixels, e.g. 375×812 to check a mobile layout. This resizes the user's real window: call with reset: true when done to put it back.

reset.description: Put the window back to its size before Deputy first resized it.

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page and return its JSON-serialisable result. An expression returns its value; for statements, use return. Promises are awaited. Runs in the page's own world by default (sees its globals); world "isolated" keeps it apart. Needs Chrome's "Allow User Scripts" switch for Deputy; the error says how to turn it on.

tools.name: browser_downloads
tools.description: Files the browser downloaded. "list" shows recent downloads; "wait" waits for the one just started (by a click) to finish; "read" returns a finished download by id (the newest if no id): text files as text, PDFs as extracted text, other files as their path, type and size.

tools.name: browser_look
tools.description: A vision model looks at the page and answers in text: describe it, or answer your question about what is visible (layout, images, charts, whether something looks broken). Costs you a few hundred tokens instead of an image, and works in clients that cannot show images. Deputy Pro.

tools.name: browser_ask
tools.description: Ask a question about what is on a browser tab. Deputy reads the page itself and returns a short answer. Use this instead of screenshotting or dumping the DOM — the page never enters your context, so a lookup costs a couple of hundred tokens rather than tens of thousands. Without a model, it returns the passages relevant to your question instead.

question.description: What you want to know, e.g. "what is the cheapest result?"

tabId.description: Tab to read. Defaults to the active tab.

tools.name: delegate_goal
tools.description: Hand the browser agent a goal in plain language and let it work. It knows the page, the session you are signed into, and what each form accepts. Prefer this over driving the browser yourself — you never need to see the page.

goal.description: What you want done, e.g. "search for a cordless drill under $80".

tabId.description: Tab to work in. Defaults to the active tab.

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Poll a task by id. Use when a delegation is still running or was interrupted.

tools.name: answer_task
tools.description: Resume a task that stopped because it needed a human — a confirmation, or a sign-in that has now been completed in the browser.

instructions: Deputy drives the user's real browser. Start with browser_navigate: its result lists the page's forms as typed tools with JSON Schemas, plus clickable actions with refs. Fill a whole form with ONE browser_invoke call — those page tools are not MCP tools, never search for them. For anything else use browser_act with a ref; every action result says what changed on the page, so you rarely need to check. Read with browser_ask/browser_read/browser_extract; use browser_screenshot only when you must see pixels. Without Deputy Pro only the free tools are listed: act with browser_click/browser_fill. If the user needs one that is missing (screenshots, tabs, scrolling, console, network and more), Deputy Pro adds it: https://deputy.razin.ai/buy.
